about.title: La Verne Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: La Verne sees its share of traffic activity along Foothill Boulevard, SR-210, Arrow Highway, and White Avenue, and not every injury on these roads or in local homes and workplaces traces back to driver error. Sometimes the real cause is a defective tire, faulty airbag, malfunctioning brake component, or a poorly designed consumer product that failed when it shouldn't have. Los Angeles County families dealing with these injuries often don't realize that California law treats these claims differently than a typical car accident case. Under strict liability, you generally don't need to prove the manufacturer was careless — only that the product was defective and that the defect caused harm. That distinction matters, because it can open the door to claims against manufacturers, distributors, and retailers alike. If a broken or dangerous product hurt you or someone you love in La Verne, keeping the item itself and documenting what happened are two of the most useful things you can do early on. LawProactive can connect you with an attorney who understands how to evaluate these claims.

whyChoose.title: Why La Verne Residents Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Strict Liability Can Simplify Your Case
items.desc: California generally lets injured people focus on whether a product was defective and caused harm, rather than proving the manufacturer was negligent. That can streamline what you need to establish from the start.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially be held liable under California law. An attorney can help identify which parties were actually involved in getting the defective product into your hands.

items.title: Preserving Evidence Matters Early
items.desc: Because these claims often hinge on the physical product itself, keeping it intact and unaltered can be critical to building a strong case. A connected attorney can advise you on how to protect this evidence right away.

items.question: Do I need to prove the manufacturer was negligent?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California's strict liability framework generally allows injured people to focus on showing the product was defective and that the defect caused their injury. This differs from many other injury claims that require proof of carelessness.

items.question: I was hurt near Foothill Boulevard when a car part failed — who could be responsible?
items.answer: It depends on what failed and why. Depending on the facts, the vehicle manufacturer, a parts supplier, or even the retailer who sold the component could potentially bear responsibility. An attorney can help sort out which party or parties were actually involved.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Try to keep it exactly as it was at the time of the injury, without repairing or discarding it. The product itself is often central evidence in these claims, and losing it can make a case much harder to pursue.
